intro:
Checking the gold price in UK today gives savers, bullion investors, and jewellery buyers an accurate benchmark in British pounds sterling. As home to the London Bullion Market, the United Kingdom sits at the heart of global precious metals clearing, and the live UK gold rate reflects both international spot trading and real-time movements in the pound sterling.

Whether you are monitoring the gold price in UK per gram today to buy VAT-free Britannia or Sovereign coins, checking the 22K gold price UK per tola and per 10 grams for bridal jewellery, or valuing hallmarked 18K and 9K pieces, our live tables and calculator above provide instant sterling breakdowns across every standard weight and purity.

sections.h2: Gold Rate in UK Today: How Live GBP Spot Prices Work per Gram and Ounce
paragraphs: London serves as the world's premier centre for wholesale physical over-the-counter gold trading, overseen by the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA). While global institutional trades are often cleared in US dollars, UK retail buyers and savers transact in British pounds sterling (GBP). The live gold rate in UK today displayed in our tables converts the real-time international benchmark directly into pounds, updating continuously as both bullion markets and sterling exchange rates move.

In everyday British commerce, metric weights take priority over imperial measures when pricing precious metals at the counter. Most UK bullion dealers, high-street jewellers, and scrap gold buyers quote the gold price in UK per gram first, followed by the troy ounce (31.1 grams) and the 1 kilogram bar (1000 grams). Our live tables also include 10-gram and traditional weights so every buyer in Britain can compare figures without manual conversions.

Always bear in mind that the live spot rate represents raw wholesale metal traded in institutional bars. When buying minted coins, small investment bars, or hallmarked jewellery in the United Kingdom, the retail price you pay includes fabrication costs, assay fees, and dealer margins above the baseline sterling spot rate.

sections.h2: Which Gold Purity to Buy in the UK: 24K, 22K, 18K, 14K, and 9K Hallmarks
paragraphs: In the United Kingdom, gold purity is strictly regulated by law and expressed in both carats and millesimal fineness marks stamped by an official UK Assay Office. For pure bullion investment, 24K gold (stamped 999 or 9999) is the universal standard for cast bars, minted bars, and contemporary Gold Britannia coins. Close behind is 22K gold (stamped 916), which is the historic crown gold alloy used for the British Gold Sovereign as well as traditional high-purity bridal and Asian jewellery sold across Britain.

For fine British luxury jewellery and engagement rings, 18K gold (stamped 750) is widely favoured for its deep, warm colour and strong resistance to tarnishing and everyday wear. Mid-range 14K gold (stamped 585) has also grown increasingly popular in modern UK boutiques, offering a practical balance between pure gold content and mechanical durability.

A defining feature of the British high street is the widespread popularity of 9K gold (stamped 375), which is the lowest legal gold purity hallmarked in the United Kingdom. Containing pure gold alloyed with harder metals like silver, copper, and zinc, 9K jewellery is exceptionally tough and affordable for everyday rings, chains, and bracelets, though its intrinsic scrap value per gram is proportionally lower than 18K or 22K pieces.
bullets: 24K (999 fine): Pure investment-grade bullion used in modern Gold Britannias and accredited refinery bars.
22K (916 fine): Historic crown gold used in British Sovereign coins and South Asian bridal jewellery across the UK.
18K (750 fine) and 14K (585 fine): Premium fine jewellery purities combining rich lustre with lasting strength.
9K (375 fine): Classic British high-street jewellery standard known for durability and accessible pricing.

sections.h2: UK VAT Exemption and Tax Advantages on Investment Gold, Britannias, and Sovereigns
paragraphs: One of the most compelling reasons British savers turn to physical bullion is the favourable tax treatment granted to qualifying investment gold in the United Kingdom. Under UK tax rules, investment-grade gold bars and qualifying bullion coins are completely exempt from Value Added Tax (VAT). This gives gold a distinct structural advantage over silver and platinum bullion in Britain, which normally attract standard VAT on retail purchases.

Beyond the VAT exemption, coins struck by The Royal Mint that hold British legal tender status—specifically the Gold Britannia and the Gold Sovereign—are classified as sterling currency for tax purposes. Because legal tender currency is exempt from UK Capital Gains Tax (CGT), UK residents can buy and sell any quantity of Gold Sovereigns and Gold Britannias without owing Capital Gains Tax on their profits, regardless of how much the uk gold rate appreciates over time.

British investors comparing bars against coins should weigh this distinction carefully. While certified 24K gold bars from accredited refiners are VAT-exempt and often carry slightly lower upfront premiums per gram on larger sizes like 100 grams or 1 kilogram, profits realised on bullion bars or foreign non-sterling coins may be subject to Capital Gains Tax if total annual gains exceed the personal allowance.
bullets: Qualifying investment gold bars and bullion coins are exempt from VAT across the United Kingdom.
Royal Mint Gold Britannias (24K) and Gold Sovereigns (22K) are UK legal tender and exempt from Capital Gains Tax for UK residents.
A British Gold Sovereign is struck in 22K crown gold and contains approximately 7.32 grams of pure gold.
Gold bars offer low fabrication premiums per gram and remain VAT-free, making them popular for vault and ISA/SIPP-style pension rules where applicable.

sections.h2: Gold Weights Used in the UK: Grams, Troy Ounces, Sovereigns, and Tolas
paragraphs: British buyers encounter a blend of metric, historic imperial, and international traditional units depending on whether they are shopping for bullion bars, Royal Mint coins, or cultural jewellery. The metric gram is the standard unit for pricing scrap gold, hallmarking thresholds, and fractional minted bars ranging from 1 gram, 5 grams, and 10 grams up to 50 grams, 100 grams, 250 grams, 500 grams, and 1000 grams (1 kilogram).

In the coin and wholesale market, the troy ounce (approximately 31.1 grams) remains the benchmark for flagship 1 oz Gold Britannia coins as well as fractional half-ounce, quarter-ounce, and tenth-ounce coins. Meanwhile, the British Gold Sovereign represents a historic weight category of its own, with a gross weight of roughly 7.988 grams of 22K gold, yielding about 7.32 grams of fine pure gold.

Across thriving jewellery quarters in London (such as Hatton Garden, Southall, Green Street, and Wembley), Birmingham's Jewellery Quarter, Leicester's Golden Mile, Bradford, and Manchester, shoppers also frequently check the 22k gold price uk per tola and per 10 grams. One tola equals approximately 11.66 grams, and our live conversion table lets British shoppers verify per-gram, 10-gram, and ounce rates side by side.

sections.h2: UK Assay Office Hallmarking: How British Purity Guarantees Protect Buyers
paragraphs: The United Kingdom operates one of the oldest and strictest statutory consumer protection systems in the world through its Hallmarking Act. By law, any gold item above 1 gram sold and described as gold in the UK must carry an official hallmark applied by one of the four independent British Assay Offices—located in London, Birmingham, Sheffield, and Edinburgh—or a recognised international convention hallmark.

A full traditional UK hallmark consists of three compulsory symbols struck directly into the metal: the sponsor's or maker's registered mark showing who submitted the item, the millesimal fineness number (such as 375 for 9K, 585 for 14K, 750 for 18K, 916 for 22K, or 999 for 24K), and the Assay Office town mark (a leopard's head for London, an anchor for Birmingham, a Yorkshire rose for Sheffield, or a three-turreted castle for Edinburgh).

Unlike self-stamping regimes in some countries where manufacturers apply their own purity marks, British Assay Offices independently test the metal using X-ray fluorescence or fire assay before laser-marking or punch-marking the piece. Every retail jeweller in the UK is also legally required to display the official Assay Office Dealer's Notice in their showroom or on their website so customers can identify every symbol with confidence.
bullets: All gold jewellery sold in the UK weighing over 1 gram must carry an independent statutory hallmark.
Look for the three compulsory marks: sponsor's initials, millesimal fineness number (375, 585, 750, 916, or 999), and Assay Office town symbol.
The four UK Assay Offices are London (leopard's head), Birmingham (anchor), Sheffield (rose), and Edinburgh (castle).
Independent assay testing ensures that 22K, 18K, and 9K pieces sold in Britain match their stated purity.

sections.h2: Why High-Street Jewellers and Bullion Dealers Charge Above the Spot Price
paragraphs: When comparing the live gold price today uk per gram on this page against a shop window in Hatton Garden or Birmingham's Jewellery Quarter, you will notice that physical items always cost more than their raw melt value. For investment coins and bars, dealers charge a percentage premium over spot to cover refining, minting or casting, Assay Office or LBMA certification, insured Royal Mail Special Delivery or courier transport, and dealer operating margins.

For hallmarked jewellery, the gap between intrinsic metal value and the retail price tag is considerably wider. Unlike investment gold, finished gold jewellery in the United Kingdom is subject to standard VAT on the full retail price. In addition, jewellers factor in design labour, stone mounting, hallmarking fees, boutique rent, insurance, and retail markups.

In specialist 22K jewellery shops across Leicester, Southall, and Birmingham, pricing is usually broken down clearly on the invoice: the live 22K store gold rate multiplied by the gram weight, plus a making charge per gram for craftsmanship, plus VAT. Checking the live 22K gold price UK per gram here before visiting a showroom helps you benchmark the base metal rate and negotiate making charges effectively.
bullets: Bullion coins and bars are VAT-free in the UK, so you only pay the live metal value plus a modest dealer premium.
Finished gold jewellery attracts UK VAT as well as craftsmanship making charges and showroom retail markups.
Smaller 1 gram and 5 gram bullion bars carry higher per-gram fabrication markups than 1 oz coins or 100 gram bars.

sections.h2: What Moves the Gold Price in the UK: Sterling, Bank of England, and Global Demand
paragraphs: The uk gold rate today is driven by two interlocking forces: the global wholesale demand for bullion and the exchange value of the British pound sterling. Because international liquidity pools clear primarily in US dollars, any weakening of the pound against the dollar automatically lifts the sterling price of gold in Britain, even if the dollar spot price remains flat. Consequently, physical gold has historically acted as a powerful hedge for UK households against sterling depreciation.

Domestic monetary policy set by the Bank of England also plays an influential role. When UK base interest rates fall or inflation erodes the real purchasing power of cash held in British savings accounts and ISAs, savers often increase allocations toward physical sovereigns, Britannias, and allocated vault gold. Conversely, rising real gilt yields can temper short-term speculative flows.

Seasonal cultural demand also shapes UK physical retail activity. During major wedding seasons and festivals such as Diwali and Eid, British jewellery districts see surging footfall for 22K sets and sovereign coins, occasionally tightening local retail availability and supporting firm dealer premiums across the country.

Bank of England interest rate decisions and UK inflation data influence domestic safe-haven demand.

sections.h2: Practical Tips Before Buying or Selling Gold in the United Kingdom
paragraphs: Before purchasing physical gold in the UK, clarify whether your priority is tax-efficient investment or wearable jewellery. If you are investing for capital growth, focus on VAT-free, CGT-exempt Royal Mint Gold Britannias and Gold Sovereigns from established UK bullion dealers. Compare the total delivered price—including insured delivery or vaulted storage fees—and check the dealer's published buy-back rate to see how narrow their spread is.

If you are buying 22K or 18K jewellery in districts such as Hatton Garden, Birmingham's Jewellery Quarter, or Leicester's Golden Mile, always inspect the piece under a loupe to confirm a genuine UK Assay Office hallmark. Ask for an itemised receipt that clearly states the karat purity, net gold weight in grams (excluding non-gold stones or clasps), the gold rate applied, the making charge, and the VAT component.

When selling old or broken 9K, 14K, 18K, or 22K jewellery for scrap, sort your items by hallmark fineness at home first and weigh each group on a digital gram scale. Use our live UK calculator above to determine the exact intrinsic sterling melt value before approaching Hatton Garden trade counters, postal gold buyers, or local jewellers so you can spot lowball offers immediately.

Prioritise UK legal tender Gold Britannias and Sovereigns if you want both VAT exemption and Capital Gains Tax exemption.

faq.q: Why is investment gold exempt from VAT in the UK?
faq.a: Under United Kingdom tax legislation, qualifying investment gold bars and bullion coins meet specific purity and market criteria that exempt them from Value Added Tax (VAT). This makes physical gold bullion significantly more tax-efficient to buy in Britain than silver bullion or retail gold jewellery, both of which attract standard VAT.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Gold Sovereign and a Gold Britannia?
faq.a: Both are official UK legal tender bullion coins struck by The Royal Mint that are exempt from VAT and Capital Gains Tax for UK residents. The Gold Sovereign is struck in durable 22K crown gold (916 fineness) and contains about 7.32 grams of pure gold, whereas modern Gold Britannias are struck in 24K pure gold (9999 fineness) and contain a full troy ounce (31.1 grams) of fine gold in the 1 oz coin.

faq.q: How do I check if UK gold jewellery has a genuine hallmark?
faq.a: Look inside the band or near the clasp for the three compulsory UK statutory marks: the sponsor's registered initials, the millesimal purity number (such as 375 for 9K, 750 for 18K, or 916 for 22K), and the symbol of one of the four UK Assay Offices (London, Birmingham, Sheffield, or Edinburgh).

faq.q: Why is 22K gold jewellery in the UK more expensive than the live 22K gram price?
faq.a: The live 22K gold price UK per gram shown in our table reflects the intrinsic wholesale metal value. Retail 22K jewellery in the UK also includes the craftsman's making charge, Assay Office hallmarking costs, showroom margins, and standard UK VAT on the finished piece.

faq.q: How is the scrap value of 9K or 18K gold calculated in the UK?
faq.a: Scrap buyers weigh your hallmarked pieces in grams and multiply the weight by the live sterling rate for that specific purity (375 parts per thousand for 9K, or 750 parts per thousand for 18K), deducting a small refining and handling margin.

faq.q: Does the British pound exchange rate affect the gold price in UK today?
faq.a: Yes. Because global wholesale gold is priced primarily in US dollars, any change in the pound sterling exchange rate immediately impacts the GBP gold price. If the pound weakens against the dollar while global gold holds steady, the gold price in the UK rises in sterling terms.

faq.q: What weights are most commonly used to buy gold in the United Kingdom?
faq.a: High-street jewellers and scrap dealers price gold per gram and per 10 grams, while bullion investors most commonly buy 1 oz Gold Britannias (31.1 grams), British Gold Sovereigns (about 7.32 grams pure gold), and minted bars in 1 gram, 10 gram, 100 gram, and 1 kilogram sizes.
